starting_branch_base: claude/zaad-meio-recovery-v6 (PR #36, V6 verdict NEEDS FURTHER MULTI-ECHELON / RECOVERY ENGINEERING)
pre_tuning_source_hash_scope: sha256 over sorted zaad/full/*.py then scripts/run_zaad_full_benchmark.py

holdout4.status: FROZEN, UNRUN, unchanged; run only if validation7 clearly qualifies and only on a later explicit instruction

split_overlap_check: development7 (36001) and validation7 (37001, 37002) do not appear in any earlier development/validation/final/holdout split above, nor in holdout4

matrix.name: v7
matrix.definition: every v6 cell unchanged (ids 0-96), then the v7 capital/recovery cells appended with new ids

v7_additions.fast_arc_pooling: central_two_branches with transfer lead 0 (same review), 1 and 2, at full and constrained capacity, with independent and correlated branch demand, and with central stock shared by both branches or short
v7_additions.recovery_A_supplier_delay: stable -> supplier lead deterioration -> recovery -> long stable tail, 30 reviews
v7_additions.recovery_B_route_closure: stable -> route closure with alternate -> reopening -> stable tail, 30 reviews
v7_additions.recovery_E_decline: demand decline -> new lower stable level, 30 reviews (single and two-branch)
v7_additions.recovery_G_false_signal: one false risk signal -> return to lean, 26 reviews

matrix.horizons: 26-32 reviews on the recovery cells; the v6 cells keep their own horizons unchanged

methods: robust (validation7, where the solver completes; timeout rows kept visible)

comparator_profiles.gated_pr30: reliability profile, decay off, v5/v6/v7 off
comparator_profiles.gated_v4: v5, v6 and v7 rules off
comparator_profiles.gated_v5: V5 engine (v6 and v7 rules off)
comparator_profiles.gated_v6: V6 engine (v7 rules off) - the direct predecessor
comparator_profiles.echelon_base_stock: independent MEIO-style echelon base stock, unchanged

targets.service: median >= ~.94; avoidable breaches <= V6 (23); p10 no material regression below .708; central+branch gains preserved near V6 (.936 / .952)
targets.inventory: total inventory materially below V6 1.67 periods; quiet inventory materially below 1.60; demand-decrease network inventory clearly lower; duplicated_buffer_units quantified against a V5/V6 baseline and reduced
targets.recovery: more than 60% of temporary-risk long-horizon cases return to LEAN (V6: 48%); median reviews-to-LEAN improved; stale temporary protection at 5/10/15 reviews clearly lower
targets.procurement: premature_purchase_units and cash_days_advanced materially lower than V6 with no service degradation attributable to delay
targets.network: central+branch median service near V6; fast-arc networks hold less total network inventory than slow-arc ones unless a physical or service constraint explains it
targets.cost: no material economic regression against V6

intended_analyses: P0 inventory decomposition per SKU/location/review with a reconciliation identity to total inventory, in units and (where meaningful) periods of demand
P1 explicit duplicated-buffer detection with the contributing buffer pair and overlap by risk source, interval, obligation, echelon and transfer accessibility
P2 fast-arc pooling audit: local immediate stock versus pooled stock computed over time
P3 demand-decrease liquidation timing and excess half-life
P4 recovery as an explicit optimization objective with the full carrying/finance/expiry/amendment burden
P5 source-specific recovery confidence and evidence counts
P6 procurement timing: earliest/latest safe order date, early inventory days, cash days advanced
P7 marginal protection value of the last protection increment
P8 inventory burden as an explicit ranked criterion in the selector
P9 bounded terminal-value treatment, evaluated on development7 and left off unless it helps
per-cell adverse-case listing and solver/timeout status, with failed comparator rows retained
rules: freeze the engine and record the SHA, config hash and seed manifest before validation7
run validation7 once; no behavioural change after validation7 results are viewed
a purely mechanical reporting/runtime defect may be corrected non-behaviourally, with the failed run preserved and the re-freeze documented
do not tune against holdout3, holdout4 or validation6; validation6 may be read only to identify already-known failure families
keep every adverse result and every timeout row; do not drop failed comparator rows from summary tables
do not achieve lean inventory by weakening service, shrinking uncertainty, deleting adverse cells, changing comparators or exploiting the finite horizon
